summary:
Infinity & Beyond is an interactive 2D retro web game that turns school-age space enthusiasts into "Space Archaeologists" rescuing the scientific legacy of inactive NASA hardware. Rather than treating silent rovers and deep-space probes as forgotten space debris, the application frames them as enduring monuments of human curiosity.

Players begin inside a Martian Deep Space Network (DSN) Hub, where they ping distant spacecraft like Voyager 1 and Pioneer 10 while experiencing simulated light-time communication delays. Next, players traverse a top-down 16-bit Martian landscape to locate dormant surface hardware including Spirit, Opportunity, and Viking 1. Approaching a rover triggers a command-line terminal interface where players diagnose real engineering faults, bypass dust-choked solar arrays or misaligned antennas, and extract dithered archival science logs. By transforming passive reading into hands-on problem-solving, the project teaches young learners how spacecraft engineering works and why the discoveries made by these weathered machines still shape planetary science today.
details:
Infinity & Beyond combines spatial 2D exploration with a command-line interface (CLI) puzzle engine across three connected gameplay phases:

  1. The Deep Space Network (DSN) Hub: From a retro-futuristic command room, players send remote pings to off-world probes (Voyager 1 and Pioneer 10). The system calculates simulated light-time delays and signal degradation to demonstrate the physical reality of communicating across billions of kilometers of interstellar space.
  2. Surface Field Excursion: Players step outside onto a top-down 16x16 pixel-art map of Mars, navigating craters and rocky terrain to locate silent hardware (Spirit, Opportunity, and Viking 1).
  3. Local Hardware "Jack-In": Approaching a rover and initiating a hardwired connection launches a full-screen green-on-black CRT terminal overlay. Players run diagnostics, resolve real historical hardware failures (such as Spirit's dust-covered solar array or Viking 1's misaligned high-gain antenna), and extract the mission's primary scientific discovery.

Under the hood, the application uses a zero-backend hybrid architecture: React 18 serves as the application shell and CLI overlay, while Phaser 3 runs inside an isolated canvas component to handle tilemap rendering and Arcade Physics collisions. A native browser CustomEvent bridge passes hardware identifiers from Phaser to React, which synchronously loads mission lore, accepted CLI commands, and dithered visual payloads from a structured hardware.json database.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Active Learning Over Passive Reading: Instead of reading an encyclopedia entry, school-age learners experience why a mission ended and how engineers troubleshoot remote spacecraft systems.
  • Accessible Anywhere: Built as a lightweight, client-side web application with zero server dependencies or installations required, the game loads instantly on standard school Chromebooks and desktop browsers.
  • Lasting Appreciation for Space Heritage: By contrasting the physical weathering of dormant machines with the permanent value of the data they sent home, the game inspires young players to see space exploration as an ongoing human story.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Coding Languages: JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5 (Canvas & DOM), CSS3, JSON.
  • Frameworks & Libraries: React 18, Phaser 3, Tailwind CSS v4, Vite.
  • Level Design & Tooling: Tiled Map Editor (orthogonal 16x16 JSON tilemaps), Git & GitHub (domain-isolated branching), Vercel (continuous deployment).
  • Hardware: Standard developer laptops running Linux and Windows environments.

Creativity & Factors Considered

  • Aesthetic & Narrative Framing: Inspired by the Japanese aesthetic of Wabi-sabi—finding beauty and historical weight in weathered, imperfect artifacts—and environmental storytelling mechanics, abandoned hardware is depicted half-buried in Martian regolith while its recovered science imagery is rendered as 16-bit dithered telemetry scans.
  • Kid-Friendly CLI Design: Because command-line interfaces can frustrate younger users, our terminal parser supports multiple command aliases per diagnostic step (e.g., accepting bypass solar, bypass --sys solar, or bypass_solar) alongside clear diagnostic hints.
  • Performance & Scope Discipline: Eliminating backend API calls prevents network latency during live classroom or judging demos and keeps asset footprints minimal.
